  `& (EXEC_SLOTS − 1)` and zero an out-of-range id by multiplication
  (`route.rs:477`, `:498`): `0xFF` and `0xFE` (`split::NO_SLOT`) index 15 and
  14 and still resolve Paper / not allowed.
- **Halt.** `HALT_FILE_MAX` 512 → 640 (`halt.rs:190`; 128 + 16 × 31 = 624).
  **Old 8-slot halt files parse unchanged**; `HaltState` is still one 64-B
  line. `apply_halt_mask` (`exec_boot.rs:505`) makes the old loop's latch
  decisions.
- **Counters.** RouteCounters 448 B; clob-dispatcher ExecCounters 1 080 B.
  **Unstamped refusals now land in the reserved slots' buckets**: `0xFF` in
  `refused_by_slot[15]`, `0xFE` in `[14]` (`counters.rs` `& 15`); at eight
  slots they landed in `[7]` and `[6]`. **Do not read buckets 14 and 15 as a
  member's number** (before S16-3, `[7]` mixed them into hcv's).
- **Ledger.** `LEDGER_RESTING` 512 → 1 024 (`ledger.rs:118`, const-asserted
  `LEDGER_RESTING / EXEC_SLOTS == 64`; core-config's mirror
  `exec.rs:423`, still const-asserted equal in `cli::exec_boot`), so the boot
  rule "a live slot's `max_open_orders` ≤ its equal share" still reads 64.
  `seeded` / `unmarked` are `SlotMask`; instrument rows 192 → 320 B; Ledger
  82 368 → 146 048 B. `INST_EXPOSURE_MAX` `i64::MAX / 512` → `/ 1024`
  (`ledger.rs:172`): a clamp only, ~$9 bn an instrument, so 1 024 rows at
  the clamp still sum inside i64 — the boundary test sums them exactly, no
  saturation.
- **The ledger high-water mark** (review). **The 1 024-row table had doubled
  every live fill / cancel / modify lookup** — scratch A/B on an M4 Pro,
  ~150 → ~280 ns warm p50 — because each occupancy scan walked the whole
  table. `resting_hi` (a u16 in existing padding, size unchanged) bounds
  every occupancy scan (locate, `working_on`, the asked-oid pass,
  `clear_resting_slot`, `drop_resting_on`) to the live prefix. Only
  `occupy` / `release` move it — the two places a row's liveness changes;
  debug builds check the invariant on every occupy / release / locate; a
  200 000-op randomized walk over slots 0..16 matches a full-table reference
  on every lookup, count and notional. **With 8 rows resting a lookup is ~3
  ns on a miss, ~7 ns on a hit**: new bench samples `ledger/locate_miss` 3.03
  ns, `ledger/locate_hit` 6.78 ns; the 20 existing samples within tolerance.
- **Boot.** core-config `live_mask` is a `SlotMask`. `exec_boot::slot_in(mask,
  slot)` (`exec_boot.rs:212`) is the one range-checked mask test (11
  readers). Compile-time guards refuse a built slot past the HL arm's
  `HL_SLOTS` (8) or Binance's `CID_SLOT_MAX` (7) until S16-4 widens them —
  otherwise a halt of a slot ≥ 8 would reach HL as a `cancel_all`.
- **The HL stop-gap until S16-4.** `cloid::HL_SLOTS = 8`
  (`exec-hyperliquid/src/cloid.rs:65`) bounds strand / `cancel_slot` / recon

### S16-4 — the venue arms (`e8ae9cd`), 2026-10-15

- **Hyperliquid:** the S16-3 stop-gap `cloid::HL_SLOTS` is gone; `decode`
  accepts a slot byte below `EXEC_SLOTS` (16 and up, and `0xFF`, still read
  Foreign); `encode` gains a `debug_assert` (its `& 15` is unreachable past
  15: the router sends a slot ≥ 16 to Paper / NoLiveRoute and the gateway's
  `admit` refuses first). recon `ALL_SLOTS` = `SlotMask::MAX`,
  `ours_on_leg(slots: SlotMask)`. `PendingSweep.slots` is a `SlotMask` in the
  old padding (u16 @28, still 36 B; `[PendingSweep; 16]` = 576 B, pinned).
  **A halt of slot s cancels only slot s's orders** (`cancel_slot` /
  `cancel_slot_state`; the stop-gap's venue-wide cancel for 8–15 is gone; a
  slot ≥ 16 keeps the venue-wide verb — unreachable, over-cancel never
  under). The gateway's `GatewayCfg.slots` / `HlGateway.slots` are
  `SlotMask`; `production()` builds its mask with
  `checked_shl(..).unwrap_or(0)` (a slot past the width owns nothing: fail
  closed); `owns_slot` bounds before it shifts and replaces the `>= 8`
  refusals in `admit` and `sweep_cancel_ours`; the arm refuses
  `cfg.slot >= EXEC_SLOTS`. The mask never crosses a process: the
  engine–gateway duplex is an in-process SPSC ring, and `HlCmd` /
  `ExecEvent` carry `slot: u8`.
- **Binance:** `cid::CID_SLOT_MAX` = `EXEC_SLOTS − 1` = 15, asserted to fit
  the cid's one hex digit (the S16-R1 ceiling); `margin::SLOTS` =
  `EXEC_SLOTS` (`MarginBook`'s arrays and the arm's `day_bought_1e6` 16 wide,
  boot-allocated). `venue_day_bought(8..15)` answers `(day, 0)` where it
  answered `None`; no route reads it.
- **A slot byte 8–15 that read Foreign now reads as that slot, and takes
  exactly the path an off-owner slot 0–7 id takes.** Hyperliquid: on a
  gateway arm an off-slot fill counts `fills_foreign` and books nothing, a
  listed order marks the account shared, `admit` refuses it; the blocking
  arm books such a fill to that slot's reconciler sheet, as it books slot
  5's; the boot / shutdown sweep cancels MV cloids as before (HL cloids
  carry no epoch). Binance (BX-9): a this-epoch off-owner id is a ghost and
  an other-epoch id an **Orphan**, as for slot 5 — cancelled by venue order
  id (never `allOpenOrders`), or the boot refused `SpotStray` / `OptStray`
  on spot / options, and an orphan's fill is booked to the owner slot
  (`TRADE_BY_ORPHAN`); before, 8–15 counted toward BX-8 drift (a halt on a
  shared account). Nothing in this engine emits 8–15 while S16-R5 holds:
  the exposure is a second engine process on the account, or a rollback
  from a build that ran a member there.
- **Byte identity:** BIN15's cloid (prefix `0x4d5603`) and the Binance cids
  of slots 0–7 are unchanged — golden tests pinned from the pre-cut
  encoders — so orders resting from before the deploy reconcile as our own.
  No persisted file has a per-slot layout (journal records carry their own
  `slot` field; anchor, budget and top-up files are per account; day-bought
  is read back from the venue), so a rollback either way reads what the
  other wrote.
- **The S16-3 compile-time guards in `exec_boot` are removed** (both arms
  now carry `EXEC_SLOTS`); the runtime S16-R5 refusal stands.
- Tests: cloid / cid round trips 0–15 and goldens; the recon, exchange and
  gateway sweeps of slot 11 never touch slot 3 (nor the `& 7` alias of a
  fixture's own slot); a 16 × 16 gateway ownership matrix; the arm takes
  8 / 11 / 15 and refuses 16+; a slot 8–15 event on a gateway arm is another
  slot's, as slot 5's; `userws` routes 11 / 15 to themselves; Binance
  off-owner and orphan ids at 5 / 10 / 11 / 15 on spot and USDⓈ-M. Gates:
  nextest 4 735 (workspace) + the review's 886 (exec-hyperliquid +
  exec-binance), alloc 127, copy-audit new 0. Review: risk SHIP WITH FIXES
  (the orphan half of the claim, the slot-11 path tests, the encode assert),

### The sweep-deferral argument at 1 024 orders (Hyperliquid; in force since S16-4)

E6 ("The invariant deferral rests on", above) sized `SWEEP_MAX_DEFERS` at
256 as four times the deferrals the largest valid configuration could need:
64 open orders on each of 8 slots, a 512-order leg. Re-derived at sixteen:

- **The largest valid leg is 16 × 64 = 1 024 of our orders.** At
  `SWEEP_CANCELS_PER_IDLE` = 8 (`exec-hyperliquid/src/exchange.rs:490`) it
  takes 1 024 / 8 = **128 calls, 127 of them deferred** (the last completes).
- The selection is truncated at `MAX_OPEN_ORDERS` = 256 (`recon.rs:466`) for
  the first (1 024 − 256) / 8 = **96 calls** — deferrals, not retries, since
  E6.
- **`SWEEP_MAX_DEFERS` = 256 (`exchange.rs:526`) is unchanged: the margin is
  now 2× (it was 4× at 512).** A genuinely stuck entry still trips the guard
  after ~256 idle moments, ~0.5 s at the 2 ms cadence; `sweep_stalled` counts
  it.
- `a_leg_larger_than_one_buffer_is_not_abandoned` (`exchange.rs:4504`)
  already sweeps a 1 024-order leg.
- Today the bound is not reachable: with 8–15 reserved no more than 8 × 64 =
  512 can be live. **Raising `max_open_orders` past 64, or the slot count past
  16, re-opens this argument** — `SWEEP_MAX_DEFERS` would be sized first.

- **`/state` schema 3** (S16-R6): `SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA` 3, `SNAPSHOT_SLOTS` =
  `MAX_STRATEGY_SLOTS`, `SLOT_NAMES` 16 (8–15 `"reserved"`, the exec_boot
  word). The name table stays a copy — depending on strategy-set would pull

  test, now over all 16 and derived from `BUILT_MASK`, is the guard.

  JSON writer already looped to `SNAPSHOT_SLOTS`: 16 slot rows, gates and
  `exec.halted` words, zero-alloc. Worst case **143 064 B** against

- paper: the `/state` halt copy is all 16 (`ex.halted = ec.halted`: a length

- `audit_pnl` labels come from `exec_boot::SLOT_NAMES` (the member table):

### The S16 deploy (2026-10-15)

`cargo build --release -p cli` at `5b56e71` (1 m 41 s); `exec-smoke
--offline` PASS (39 rows, 9 encoders); on the new binary
`multivenue-engine strategy-mask ai+vrp+xsd+bin15+hyparb+xmm+hcv` →

## HK, part 4 — Hyperliquid's parse errors and the u32 `venue_seq` (2026-10-16)

**Ask (Anton):** "HL parse errors … venue_seq on Binance, Bybit and MEXC is
still truncated to u32". **Plan:** project doc
`claude/hk-part4-plan-2026-10-16.md`. **Commits:** `fba0c3c` HK36,
`0968414` HK37; this section and the migration entries are HK38.

| id | ruling (operator, 2026-10-16) |
|---|---|
| HK-R22 | `venue_seq` for Binance / Bybit / MEXC: HK31/HK32's `ArrivalSeq`, keyed on the venue's FULL u64 id; the book sees an ordinal; a backward id takes 0 and is counted; `TopOfBook` untouched; captures carry the ordinal from the deploy on. |
| HK-R23 | The HL rejects tap: `RAW_TAP=pm,hl` (rejects only) at once, with an off-grid restart (04:16:05Z; backup `strategy.conf.bak-20261016T0413Z-hk-hltap`). It stays on: a rejects-only tap costs its 64-B header while nothing is rejected. |
| HK-R24 | HL parse errors: fix as a cut if the cause is clear (as HK-R17). |
| HK-R25 | Deploy, then push. |

### HK36 — the arrival ordinal keyed on the venue id (`fba0c3c`)

- **Why it was a live hazard.** `Tick.venue_seq` is a `u32`;
  `book_builder::TopOfBook::apply` drops `venue_seq <= last` as `Stale`.
  Binance (`bookTicker` `u`), Bybit (`orderbook.1` `u`) and the MEXC book
  (`version`) put their u64 id's low 32 bits there, and those ids are far
  past 2^32 (2026-10-16 REST: Binance USDⓈ-M BTCUSDT 11 833 358 963 074,
  ~2 755 wraps; spot 101 509 388 118; MEXC spot 83 810 244 855, futures
  42 677 422 185; Bybit linear 1 253 051, restarted after a venue
  restart). At a low-32 wrap the instrument would be `Stale` in every book
  until a restart. No member of the set reads these books today (HK32
  review), so nothing was lost yet.
- **The law.** `ArrivalSeq` takes a generic u64 key (`last_ms` →
  `last_key`, same compare) and gains a per-row `reset_clock`
  (`reset_clocks` loops it); Polymarket, Hyperliquid and Deribit are
  byte-identical. Binance: one sequencer per Driver (each connection is one
  symbol). Bybit: `[ArrivalSeq; 64]` by table row; every `snapshot` zeroes
  its symbol's clock without counting (`u` restarts at 1 under one after a
  venue restart; the clock then holds the snapshot's `u`, so a backward
  delta after it is still caught). MEXC: `[ArrivalSeq; 16]` by row (a power
  of two, asserted), stamped on every parsed book push, so republications
  feed the check and their ordinals skip. Reconnect → `reset_clocks` on all
  three. Same-id re-pushes take the next ordinal — the same touch: 2.1 % of
  Binance ticks used to be dropped as `Stale` and now apply.
- **MEXC's book check moved** from Q-MX1's last-seen compare to the
  sequencer: a version behind the NEWEST counts on every push, and an
  absent version counts (its tick was 0 and dropped silently before — now
  an alarm). The trade check is unchanged; `ChannelEvent.venue_seq` keeps
  the full u64.
- **Exhaustion.** A u32 ordinal at Binance's busiest ~810 ticks/s lasts ~61
  days of process uptime; daily-restart boots a new process five times a
  day, so the bound is unreachable in operation (documented at the
  `debug_assert`).
- **Captures and replay.** The `Tick` row carries the ordinal; the venue
  book id is in no capture row (only in raw-tap frames when the tap is on).
  Replaying several runs as one stream restarts the ordinal per run without
  a rebase: a `MultiBook` reader (latency-arb, cross-arb, rule-tree — all
  outside the set) would drop a later run's ticks until its ordinal passes
  the earlier run's.
- **Not changed (rulings):** OKX `seqId as u32`
  (`ingress-okx/src/run_loop.rs:1124`; BTC-USDT-SWAP seqId
  346 500 248 290, already past 2^32, and OKX may reset it after
  maintenance); Binance options ticks carry `venue_seq` 0, which every book
  drops as `Stale`. Both ruled and fixed the same day: HK39 / HK40 ("HK,
  part 5").
- Review: risk / alloc SHIP WITH FIXES, applied (the `paper.rs` COPY sizes —
  Bybit 6 512 B, MEXC 3 264 B — a MEXC row `debug_assert`, the replay
  note). Captured before the deploy: 0 regressions in 2 M Binance, 145 k
  Bybit and 29 k MEXC ticks.

### HK37 — Hyperliquid's empty `trades` snapshot (`0968414`)

- **Finding (the rejects tap, 04:16–04:46Z):** `parse_errors_total` and the
  tap agreed record for record — 16 — and all 16 were the same 30 bytes,
  `{"channel":"trades","data":[]}`: the venue's empty trades SNAPSHOT on a
  `trades` subscribe to a HIP-4 outcome leg that has not printed. 4 at
  boot, up to 6 a 15-minute roll (3 live families × 2 fresh legs; the 04:45
  roll was predicted at +6 and moved 10 → 16), up to 8 at the 06:00Z daily
  roll: the long-standing ~21/h. The frame classifies as `Data(Trades)` but
  names no `coin`, so the lookup failed and the catch-all
  (`run_loop.rs:1957`) counted it and tapped it. Valid, empty venue data;
  nothing lost — but the counter hid any real reject.
- **Fix (HK1's unsubscribe-echo model):** `is_empty_data_array` (lib.rs,
  beside `extract_coin`: `"data":`, JSON whitespace, `[`, whitespace, `]`;
  borrowing, zero-alloc), asked only once the coin lookup has failed, so a
  push that resolves pays nothing new → `Dispatch::TradesEmpty`: a message
  and `HlRollStatus::trades_empty`, published as
  `engine_ingress_hyperliquid_trades_empty_total`; not a parse error, not a
  reject. A broken array, rows for an unconfigured coin and an empty array
  on any other channel still count and tap. Tests: the tap's 30 bytes ×16
  (0 parse errors, 16 empty, no tick, no print), the negatives, a normal
  push unchanged; the HL frame fuzzer 60 s, 2.95 M runs, clean.

## PVM — slot 8, paper only (operator ruling 2026-10-16)

**Ruling (operator, 2026-10-16):** the Pine member (`crates/strategy-pine`, PVM impl-08 —
third-party Pine scripts, every order through `pine-broker`'s `NativeBroker`) takes **slot 8,
PAPER ONLY**: it is refused in every live arm. The running engine's `~/multivenue` configs,
wrapper and `strategy.conf` are untouched. The live venues for a later ruling are Binance and
Hyperliquid (O-PVM-2). Lead ruling: `all` keeps meaning the eight production members.

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| member table | nine rows; slot 8 = `pine` (`strategy_set::SLOT_PINE`, `BIT_PINE` 0x0100), no `regime.toml` label |
| `strategy_set::BUILT_MASK` | **0x01FF** (the OR of the rows; `StrategySet::new` clamps to it) |
| `strategy_set::ALL_MASK` | **0x00FF = `--strategy all`**, unchanged; pine is selectable by name only (`…+pine`) |
| slots 9–15 | still RESERVED: S16-R5's refusal (`(artifact \| flag) & !BUILT_MASK`) names them |
| unattributed fills | `UNATTRIBUTED_FILL_MASK = BUILT_MASK & !BIT_PINE`: slot 8 receives only fills attributed to it |
| surfaces | `/state` slot 8 reads `"pine"` (schema 3, additive — the HC11 precedent); audit-pnl labels it `pine`; the tui shows it as a member row |

**The refusals — each fail-closed, each on its own:**

1. **Parse.** `core_config::exec` refuses `[exec.slot.8] mode = "live"` before any other live
   rule, whatever its name, venues or `[exec.slot.8.pine]` say. The `[exec.slot.8.pine]` section
   (impl-08 §4.8: `min_coalesce_ms`, `event_insn_budget`, `boot_exit_policy`, …) is recognised
   only at slot 8, after `[exec]`, once; its refusals start with their code (`6004` unknown key,
   `6006` out of range, `6005` missing on Live). Without it the artifact parses exactly as
   before.
2. **Boot (`cli::exec_boot::resolve`).** `(artifact live mask | --arm-live) & PAPER_ONLY_MASK`
   (= `BIT_PINE`) refuses FIRST — before the S16-R5 check and before the interlock compare — so
   `--arm-live 8` is refused beside any artifact. The per-slot table build refuses a Live mode
   at `PINE_SLOT` on its own as well.
3. **AI plane.** `EnableStrategy(8)` is refused and counted (`enable_refused`): the AI never
   arms third-party code. `DisableStrategy(8)` and `HaltRequest` are honoured.
4. **The T19 boot — `--pine <manifest>` is required both ways (F19).** Slot 8 boots in PAPER
   only, and only with `--pine`. The set arm boots `requested & configured`, so without this
   check `ai+pine` would boot as `ai`, silently. The `run` command checks it in `Cmd::Run`, before
   `run` is entered: before the config load, the ingress threads, the exec artifact and every live
   or gateway arm (`cli::pine_boot::check_run`, exit 1). Each of these refuses: a `--strategy`
   naming pine without `--pine`; `--pine` without pine in the mask; `--pine` beside a `--strategy`
   that is not a set mask (a legacy arm such as `ev` or `rule-tree`, or a typo,
   `pin:08-run-legacy-strategy-refused`). `strategy-mask` still resolves the name (`pine` →
   `256\tpine`), so a `STRATEGY` naming it passes the wrapper and the boot decides. The
   unconfigured member's own `on_start` refuses too (F19). A configured boot (`pine_boot::build`,
   then the member's load) holds each of the following, fail-closed:
   - **Facts come from venue discovery** (operator ruling R-08-T19-1, 2026-10-17,
     `pin:08-facts-from-discovery`). Every route symbol's `PineSymbolFacts` is read from the boot
     REST discovery the run already performs: Hyperliquid `meta` `szDecimals`, Binance
     `exchangeInfo` filters. A missing fact refuses the boot. There is never a default.
   - **Slot 8's route is paper or off.** It is the router's resolved row (`ExecBoot::slots`). A
     live slot 8 never reaches here (refusals 1–2).
   - **Paper boots flat.** A non-empty `boot_state` off Live is refused (`6013`,
     `pin:08-boot-state-live-only`).
   - **The boot adoption is asserted at both ends (I38).** `reconcile_boot` silently changes
     nothing on a broker that is no longer pristine, and a flat adoption cannot be told from a
     skipped one by the position alone (risk review r15). So `arm::adopt` asserts
     `NativeBroker::is_pristine()` BEFORE `reconcile_boot` (a sequencing defect of the member
     otherwise), and after it that the adoption took: no longer pristine, the venue's position
     and, when not flat, its average price on the book. Both are `assert!` in every build.
   - **`oid_epoch != 0`.** An epoch of 0 is refused at load (`6006`, `pin:08-epoch-zero-refused`).
     With epoch 0, every own fill decodes as a prior boot's and paper re-fires without bound. The
     epoch is the boot's UTC second.
   - **The 2^29 broker-oid bound** (`1 ≤ oid < 2^29`, what the client oid can carry) is an
     `assert!` in every build, not a `debug_assert!` (`host::dispatch_one`, impl-08 §4.6).
   - **No slot-8 order carries `ORDER_FLAG_POST_ONLY`** (`pin:08-no-post-only-paper`). The bit
     selects the paper queue law, under which a cancel or modify `Ok` means only "sent". Slot 8
     settles on `Ok`, and with the bit it would share xmm's 32-order / 8-symbol queue table.
     `ORDER_KIND_MAKER` keeps the strict-cross law.
   - **`ORDER_FLAG_REDUCE_ONLY` goes on reducing orders only** (the broker's reduce-only sizing:
     exits, closes, the D13 flatten, the guards' `CloseAll`; `pin:08-order-flags-set`). The
     paper matcher ignores the bit, so on paper the broker's sizing is the guard. Live, it is a
     second guard against a flip: the exec router reads it on a Hyperliquid perp row (only a
     flagged reduction is an exit there, "B'4" below), and both arms send it to the venue —
     exec-hyperliquid on a perp row (`r: true`), exec-binance on USDⓈ-M (r28 risk review B2, C4).
   - **`activation_ns` is taken from the matcher's table** (`pin:08-activation-from-matcher-table`,
     found by G5). It is `core_fill::ACTIVATION_NS_DEFAULT[..8]`, the table `PaperMatcher` judges
     by. With zeros, an IoC was reported cancelled and then filled.

**`[exec] enabled = 0`** (`pin:08-exec-boot-resolved`). Slot 8's route is the router's resolved
row (above). Under `[exec] enabled = 0` that row is the paper default: `[exec.slot.8]`'s mode
(including `off`), caps and venues are ignored; only `[exec.slot.8.pine]` still applies.
`enabled = 0` disarms live, it does not stop slot 8: to stop it, drop pine from `STRATEGY` (and
`--pine`) or `DisableStrategy(8)`.

**Fees and bar marks.** R7 bar marks (`take_bar_marks`, `pin:08-bar-marks-replay-only`) and R8
noted fees (`note_fill_fee`) are replay-host only: the B'3 harness drains the marks and notes
each fill's fee; the engine records no marks and notes no fee. Engine paper books every slot-8
fill at the `[exec.slot.8.pine]` fee model (`fee_taker_ppm` / `fee_maker_ppm`), rounded up
(`fills::model_fee_1e12`). A negative noted fee aborts in every build, never clamped
(`pin:08-noted-fee-non-negative`); a note naming another fill books the model and is counted
in release (`noted_fee_mismatched`, `pin:08-noted-fee-one-fill`).

**No rollback door is needed.** No live order from slot 8 can exist (refusals 1–3), so an
older binary never meets a slot-8 cloid or cid; S16-R5's door stays shut. Slot 8's live-arming
ruling must reopen this.

**The pine-broker requote cap (`pin:05-requote-replaces-prev`; operator ruling 2026-10-17:
ACCEPTED).** A requote is one `Modify` (E-7). An increasing `Modify` is judged in gates 5–6
with `prev`'s unfilled quantity **replaced** by the new size, not added to it
(`outstanding − prev + new`). Every other outstanding order still counts, a `Replaced`
predecessor included. **The documented bound:** exposure may exceed `cap_instance` (and
`cap_day`) only by `prev`'s fill that is in flight when the `Modify` lands, which is at most
`prev`'s unfilled quantity. Reducing requotes are unchanged (`new ≤ |pos| − R`, with `prev`
still in `R`). Counting `prev` beside its own replacement refused every requote at a
`cap_instance` of one unit and turned each into Cancel + Submit. **Re-review this before any
live pine route.** The spec text is impl-05 §4.12.4 rule 4 and I39 (amendment AMEND-05).

**The pine-broker day roll.**
- `pin:05-boot-day-seed-kept` (R-08-T16-1): the first roll, with no adopted day, adopts its UTC
  day and keeps the `reconcile_boot` seed. Zeroing the seed there let a restart spend the day
  cap twice.
- `pin:05-roll-day-forward-only`: an earlier day never rolls. A stale event therefore cannot
  zero the day notional or lift a day-scoped halt, and its notional counts toward the adopted
  day.
- **Open — FIX-BEFORE-LIVE:** a forward jump caused by one future-stamped venue fill still rolls
  the day. That zeroes the day notional and lifts a day-scoped halt early. Before any live pine
  route, cap a forward roll at the event clock's day.

**B'1 trade routing.** Trade events reach slot 8 only. `StrategySet::on_venue_event` hands a
`ChannelId::Trade` event to the pine member, when it is enabled, and returns before the regime
tap and the member fan-out. Every other member's event stream is therefore byte-identical to
the pre-B'1 one (xmm's prints ride their own `TradePrint` lane).
- An ingress sheds a routed print, and counts it once, when the event ring is at
  `EVENT_RING_SIZE − EVENT_TRADE_RESERVE` or fuller. Since
  `EVENT_TRADE_RESERVE = EVENT_RING_SIZE / 4`, a Trade burst always leaves room for every
  non-trade channel (Funding, AssetCtx, Mark, InstrumentRoll).
- Any non-zero `engine_ingress_<venue>_trade_shed_total` is an alert, and it makes that session
  ineligible for 8g.
- The route is EMPTY, so no lane pushes a Trade for slot 8, unless `--pine` names route
  symbols. A route symbol on a lane without Trade capture refuses (`6006`).
- The commit that wires the route into the boot carries its own risk review.

**Observability.** *Amended 2026-10-17 (lead ruling, pin:08-drain-outside-metrics):* slot 8's
durable outputs — the T18 tapes (`seq.bin`, `decisions.bin`, `set.tsv`) and `incidents.log` —
drain on every 5 s block beside the loop hook's drain, OUTSIDE the metrics gate, and once more
after the loop's last iteration (before `eng.stop()`), with or without `--metrics`: they are
capture durability, not an observability option. Only the `engine_pine_*` mirror stays inside the
`/metrics` block; a pine boot without `--metrics` mirrors nothing. Tests: `cli` `pine_metrics`
`metrics_off_boot_still_drains_incidents_and_tapes`,
`engine_loop_drains_pine_outside_the_metrics_gate`.
*Amended 2026-10-17 (risk r21 #3, `pin:08-tape-buffered`):* the tapes exist only with
`--pine-tape`. Each engine-thread writer (`seq.bin`, `decisions.bin`, `set.tsv`,
`pine-delivery.bin`) is a 64 KiB `BufWriter` allocated when it opens at boot. A 5 s pass costs
one flush per file, plus a write(2) per full 64 KiB buffer, and no fsync; the final drain flushes
too. A write or flush error is logged at ERROR; it never stops the engine. *Amended 2026-10-17
(risk r23 B3):* what "void" means per file. The tapes' cursors move per record written and the
buffer keeps unwritten bytes, so a later pass retries without duplicates; a failure that persists
leaves a shorter tape (8g-A red, or an honest shorter window). The delivery journal is voided by
a file: see `pine-delivery.void` below. *Amended 2026-10-17 (risk r24):* voiding costs the 5 s
pass once per boot, and only on that failure: `void()` opens the marker `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`
(`create_new`), makes a few small unbuffered writes with no fsync, and drops the journal writer
(one last flush attempt, the close, and the free of its 64 KiB buffer and 8 KiB drain slice).
On the write-error branch the marker's `write\t<error>` line formats the OS error, which may
allocate once (the existing `error = %e` log line on that branch already did). Every later pass
skips the journal.

**The boot record and `pine-verify` (risk review r21, 2026-10-17).**
- **`<run>/pine-boot.tsv`** (`# pvm-boot-1`) is written once, atomically, right after
  `eng.start()`. It carries the boot's per-symbol facts, `queue_syms` (every symbol the paper
  queue law tracks at this boot), `exec_sha256` (the SHA-256 of `exec.toml`'s bytes, zeros
  without `--exec`) and `boot_utc_ms` (the live tape's label, `pin:08-boot-record-boot-utc-ms`).
  The parse is strict: a record missing any of these fails closed. A failed write is logged at
  ERROR, never refused; that run then cannot be replayed from boot.
- **Queue symbols.** The boot reaches the queue law only through one call that also keeps the
  symbol. The kept list goes to slot 8's hook after every member block, so the record cannot
  miss one, whatever the block order (r21 #4).
- **`<run>/pine-delivery.bin`** (R6) is written with `--pine-tape` only. Raw 32 B records,
  append-only; a gap voids the window. *Amended 2026-10-17 (risk r23 B3,
  `pin:08-delivery-void-file`, `pin:08-delivery-cursor-per-record`):* the cursor moves per record
  written, so a retried drain never writes a record twice. A gap or a write / flush error closes
  the journal for the rest of the boot and creates `<run>/pine-delivery.void` once
  (`create_new`; `# pvm-delivery-void-1`, then `gap\t<n>` or `write\t<error>`).
  `backtest --replay-from-boot` refuses a `--delivery-journal` with that file beside it, exit 6,
  before any record. *Amended 2026-10-17 (risk r24, `pin:08-delivery-journal-canonical`):* it
  first resolves `--delivery-journal` with `std::fs::canonicalize` (a path that does not resolve
  is refused, exit 6), looks for the marker beside the resolved file, and reads that file. The
  guarantee is exactly this, with two limits:
  - **A copied journal carries no marker.** The marker is looked up beside the journal's
    canonical path only, so a symlink to the run's journal is judged by the run's marker, but a
    journal COPIED elsewhere (into a hand-built window root beside `pine-boot.tsv`, say) is read
    as if whole. `--delivery-journal` must be the live run's own `<run>/pine-delivery.bin`.
  - **A marker that cannot be created is only logged**: ERROR `pine: delivery void marker NOT
    written` (with `error` and `path`), after the ERROR that voided the journal; the run goes on.
    The records carry no journal ordinal, so nothing else on disk marks that hole: those two log
    lines are then the only record that the journal is void.
- **`pine-verify` is offline and read-only.** It opens no socket, reads no `.env` and arms
  nothing. It replays on its own slot-8-only `PaperMatcher`. An armed `exec.toml` is loaded under
  its own arming: rule 3 is a re-hash of the bytes against `exec_sha256`, never the two-switch
  interlock (r21 #1).
- **What makes a window ineligible.** Listed with its reason, never counted, never red:
  - a pine symbol that is also in `queue_syms` (`pin:08-verify-queue-sym-ineligible`);
  - rules 4/6 that cannot be shown: no `set.tsv` rows, a row gap over 10 s, a short row, or a
    non-zero `rejected_open_cap`.
- **What is red.** A fill the replayed matcher still holds after the replay counts as a diff
  (r21 #2).
- **Replay tapes never append.** `backtest --replay-from-boot --tape-out` names its tape directory
  from the record's `boot_utc_ms` and creates every file new. An existing tape is refused with
  exit 2 (r21 #5). `pine-verify --cross` therefore pairs live and replay tapes exactly.

**8g-B pairing and the output paths (risk review r22, 2026-10-17).**
- **The pairing rule (B1, N1).** `pine-verify --cross <root>` pairs the live tape
  `tape/<boot_utc_ms>/` with `<root>/<boot_utc_ms>/`, made by
  `backtest --replay-from-boot --fills recorded --tape-out <root>` over that boot's run (same
  label, same `oid_epoch`). Each of the following makes the window ineligible: listed with its
  reason, never counted, never red.
  - No tape under the label (rule 7).
  - A seq gap in either replay tape.
  - A replay `BOOT_HDR` that does not read route Paper, host Replay, and the live header's
    `oid_epoch` and `boot_utc_ms`; or a live header whose host is not Engine. The live tape is
    never paired with itself (`pin:08-cross-pair-is-replay`).
  - A replay made in the other mode. `--tape-out` writes `replay.tsv` (`# pvm-replay-1`, then
    `fills\t<mode>`), created new. 8g-B pairs with `recorded` only. Absent, malformed or
    `judged` is ineligible (`pin:08-cross-replay-fills-file`). *Amended 2026-10-17 (risk r23
    B2, `pin:08-replay-file-after-clean-drive`):* `replay.tsv` is written last, after the final
    flush, and only by a drive that finished clean. A replay that faulted (exit 4), diverged
    (exit 5) or aborted on an I/O error has tapes but no `replay.tsv`; its window is ineligible
    ("unrecorded or unfinished replay"). impl-08 §4.9 names no mode;
    impl-Bp §4.12 recommends `recorded` as the member-determinism gate
    (`pin:08-cross-fills-recorded`).
  - Different `BOOT_SCRIPT` sets on the two tapes (`pin:08-cross-boot-scripts`).
- **Four tape fields are NOT compared (N2, `pin:08-cross-fields-listed`).** A pair is equal iff
  the fields impl-08 §4.9.1 lists for its kind are equal. `DISPATCH`: a, b, c, bar, oid, px,
  qty, id, previous oid. `DISPOSITION`: a, oid. `FILL`: oid, px, signed qty, fee, `time_ms`.
  The four fields outside those lists:
  - `DISPOSITION.b`, the rule. It is the host's: 1 (paper evidence) live, 3 on the replay.
  - `FILL.a`, the origin. It is the host's.
  - `FILL.b`, the side. The signed qty carries it.
  - `FILL.bar_index`. §4.9.1's `FILL` list names no bar.

  8g-B cannot see a difference in these four.
- **The wall anchor (`pin:08-boot-record-anchor`, lead ruling R3; retires
  `pin:Bp-recorded-wall-map`).** The boot record carries the live member's wall anchor, exact
  in ns. The replayed member runs on the identity anchor. The harness maps every record and
  journal stamp onto the live anchor: `wall = anchor_wall + (ts − anchor_mono)`. The
  `BOOT_HDR` anchor words (x0, x1) are therefore not compared.
- **`set.tsv` must cover the window (C1, `pin:08-set-rows-span`).** Rules 4/6 hold only when
  all of the following do; else the window is ineligible.
  - Rows strictly increase, each at most 10 s after the one before (`0 < d ≤ 10 000` ms,
    overflow-checked).
  - The first row is at most 10 s after the boot.
  - The last row is at least `min(boot + 2 h, last in-window seq record's wall) − 10 s`. With
    no seq record, the boot stands in.
  - Every row has slot 8's bit set, and every row reads `rejected_open_cap` 0 (a short row
    fails).
- **`--report-out` and `--tape-out` refusals (C2, C3).** Each path is judged on its canonical
  form (`pin:08-out-canonical`): the longest existing prefix goes through `canonicalize`, which
  follows every symlink; the remainder is applied lexically. A dangling link cannot be
  resolved: exit 6.
  - Inside a git working tree, a symlink into one included: exit 6.
  - A report under `~/multivenue/` but not under `~/multivenue/pine/` (both canonical): exit 6
    (`pin:08-report-out-pine-only`).
  - An existing report: exit 2, before any record. The one write is `create_new`, so a report
    is never overwritten (`pin:08-report-out-create-new`).
  - The replay's default report, `~/multivenue/pine/8g/<run>.jsonl`, is checked the same way.
  - `--tape-out` gets the git refusal only, not the pine-only rule (risk r23): a tape under the
    live root `~/multivenue/pine/tape/` is accepted. Harmless: every file is created new (an
    existing label exits 2, never appended), and a replay tape carries host Replay, so rule 1
    (host Engine) makes a window read from it ineligible.
  - `--report-out` belongs to the pine arms only (`--strategy pine`, `--replay-from-boot`). The
    legacy ruleset arm refuses it at parse (C4, `pin:Bp-8g-report-out-shared`).
- **The live tape is created new (`pin:08-live-tape-create-new`; retires the live
  create-or-append).** The live `--pine-tape` creates every file under
  `~/multivenue/pine/tape/<boot_utc_ms>/` new. A second boot on the same label, or a clock
  stepped back onto an earlier one, finds the files (a dangling link counts). That boot's tapes
  are then OFF, with one ERROR line (`pine: --pine-tape not opened — tapes OFF for this boot,
  window void`). Nothing is appended to the earlier tape. The boot itself never fails because
  of a tape: `incidents.log` still appends and the member runs.

**Bench.** `bench/benches/hot_path.rs` builds `StrategySet::new(BUILT_MASK)`, so
`strategy_set/on_tick_all` now includes the inert pine member (one branch and one counter); a
`bench-check` drift there is this, and the re-baseline is the operator's.

**Re-baselined in the r40 merge (2026-10-29, ruling R-P35).** Merging main `df543c33` (pm15 slot 9,
pmj slot 11) into the branch made pine one of eleven built rows: `strategy_set/on_tick_all` 4.63 →
5.87 ns and `on_tick_none` 3.06 → 3.32 ns (one cycle). Evidence: an interleaved A/B, six rounds of the
`strategy_set` benches with bench-check's settings, A = main `df543c33`, B = the merged tree, both

B 3.31 ns; `on_timer_all` and `on_fill_routed` unmoved. The rounds and the values' derivation are in
`crates/bench/baselines/hot_path.json`. A set-bit fan-in (cost by enabled members, not built rows)
stays the possible later lane.

## B'4 — Hyperliquid perps (impl-Bp §4.13–§4.14; DARK until the operator arms it, 2026-10-17)

**Status: written BEFORE any perp arms** ("no subsequent E-phase may arm a venue without its own
entry here first", "Phased loosening"). A perp is a new instrument class on the armed venue.
**Nothing arms by default:** slot 8 (Pine) stays PAPER ONLY — refusals 1–3 of "PVM — slot 8,
paper only" stand unchanged, and the cli never sets the PL2 live permit. The code below builds and
judges the perp half of a boot; wiring it into a live boot and arming are the operator's acts.
`risk-reviewer` closes this entry before R2. **OPEN until then.**

**Risk review 2026-10-29 (r40, R-P32 "Paperwork only") — NOT CLOSED.** The laws below (E-4P,
refuse-never-round, isolated margin, one owner per coin, the three cap laws, recon) hold for the
code that exists (`exec_hyperliquid::perp`, `perp_recon`, `cli::pine_hl`, `exec_boot::boot_hl_perps`).
Blocking before it can close (vault `pvm/live/risk-review-2026-10-29.md`,
`pvm/live/hl-overlap-2026-10-29.md`):
- **RH-1** T0.6 (the E7 anchor with the perp `accountValue`) is unanswered — arming is blocked by
  this entry's own text.
- **RH-2** **The perp-overlap rule does not cover slot 8.** `xmm_live::check_perp_overlap` lists
  hyparb, vrp and hcv as slot 6's others; no check compares slot 8's perps with slot 6's quotes or
  the hedges, in either direction. And no in-engine check can see the standalone engines
  (XMM on EC2, HYPARB on EC2, BIN15 on the Mac) that trade Hyperliquid on their own accounts.
  Required at the arming change: slot 8 in both directions of the overlap check, and **a Hyperliquid
  account (master or sub-account) used only by slot 8**, never one another engine or slot trades.
- **RH-3** The pine perp path is not assembled: `boot_hl_perps`, `pine_hl::hl_perp_boot` /
  `seed_router_perps` / `live_rows_from_hl` are called by tests only; slot 8 has no gateway arm,
  no `NonceStreams` stream and no dead-man binding. The review re-runs on the assembled boot.

**LAW E-4P.** A perp asset id is valid only when bound at THIS boot from the venue's own `meta`
answer, by exact coin name, from an entry that is not delisted; never derived, never carried
across a boot (`exec_hyperliquid::perp::PerpTable::bind_from_meta`). Refused at boot: a coin
absent from `meta`, delisted, leverage 0 or above its `maxLeverage`, a coin or symbol routed
twice. Perps do not roll; the boot binding replaces E-4's roll binding. One boot tell per coin
(`perp coin=… asset=… szDecimals=… maxLev=… lev=… min=$…`): read the asset id off it.

**Refuse, never round.** A perp order whose price breaks the venue grid (more than 5 significant
figures and not an integer, or more than `6 − szDecimals` decimals), whose size has more than
`szDecimals` decimals, or whose value is below the coin's minimum is refused locally before
signing (`perp::check`; counted in `refused_local` and per `PerpRefusal`). Nothing is rounded.
impl-08's tick is `perp::tick_1e6(ref, szDecimals)`; past that price decade an off-grid limit is
refused, never rounded.

**The minimum.** `min_notional_1e6 = max($10 documented, the probe's value)`. The probe file
(`~/multivenue/hl-perp-limits.tsv`, written by `scripts/exec-smoke.sh --perp-probe`, testnet) is
an **arming precondition**: a coin absent from it cannot arm (`exec_boot::hl_perp_wants`). The
slot's `max_order_usd_1e6` must clear every routed coin's minimum or no order passes both
(impl-08 `6009`).

**Isolated margin, leverage fixed at boot.** `[exec.hl_perp] isolated = 1` is required (any other
value refuses the boot); `updateLeverage {asset, isCross: false, leverage}` once per coin at boot,
a non-`default` answer refuses the boot; leverage never changes at runtime. A venue position that
is not isolated, or whose leverage differs from `exec.toml`, refuses the boot. One coin's loss
cannot consume another's margin.

**One owner slot per coin.** A bound perp coin has exactly one `owner_slot`; another slot's order
is refused (`NotOwner`). impl-08 allows one enabled script per (venue, coin) on Live (`6007`).

**The three cap laws for a perp row (O-E4: caps stay exactly paper's).**
- `max_order_usd` = `px × qty`, unchanged; `max_open_orders` unchanged — it counts every PLACE,
  an exit's too (O-BX25).
- **An EXIT** is a pure reduction (its opening part 0) that carries `ORDER_FLAG_REDUCE_ONLY`; the
  arm sends the flag to the venue (`r: true`, submit and modify), so N stacked exits cannot flip
  the coin — the venue refuses what would. An exit is exempt from `max_order_usd` alone (L1, "a
  cap never blocks an exit"). A reduction without the flag is judged by every clamp, inside the
  stated worst case `cap_instance + max_open_orders × max_order` (r28 risk review B2;
  `pin:bp4-perp-exit-exempt-clamp-1`).
- `cap_instance_usd` = `Σ |pos| × price` over the slot's perp rows. The order's coin is priced at
  the order's limit on BOTH sides of the test; every other row at its last fill. Refused iff
  `projected > cap && projected > current`: a reduction is never refused.
- `cap_day_usd` = filled OPENING notional (the part of a fill that increases `|pos|`, either
  side); a reduction adds nothing, so exiting stays always possible.
- A perp fill books to its row, never `fills_unbound`.

**Reconciliation and halts.** Each recon cycle reads `clearinghouseState` (counted by the budget
governor); drift = `Σ |ledger pos − szi| × px` (USD ×1e6) against `halt_on_recon_drift_usd_1e6`
— a sticky halt; `halt_on_recon_stale_ms` unchanged. The boot seeds each row from
`clearinghouseState` and today's opening notional from `userFillsByTime` (00:00Z, paged). **The
anchor extension (T0.6):** the E7 P&L halts must include the perp `accountValue` before a perp
arms — until T0.6 answers, arming is blocked. What stops it: `exec.HALT`, the E6 halts, the
drift and stale halts, the E7 bound; **a cancel is never blocked by a cap** (E6).

**Fees.** Measured from `userFills.fee` after the first live fills; an arming decision reads a
measured row (§4.10).

**What the operator must do to arm (none of it is done by code):**
1. Run `scripts/exec-smoke.sh --perp-probe --perp-coins <coins> --perp-leverage <lev>` on the
   TESTNET account (after phases A and B); exit 0, and `hl-perp-limits.tsv` lists every coin to
   arm. Exit 67: a coin's answers did not match the documented rules (it is left out); exit 68:
   something may be LEFT ON THE TESTNET ACCOUNT — read and clear it. `--perp-probe --offline` is
   the cost-free self-test.
2. `[exec.hl_perp]` in `exec.toml` (`isolated = 1`, `leverage`, `limits`), the slot's caps at
   paper's (O-E4) with `max_order_usd_1e6 ≥` every coin's minimum.
3. T0.6 answered and the anchor extension reviewed; impl-08's R0–R4 ramp, **R2 the first perp
   signature on mainnet**, one coin, the smallest size.
4. The live-arming ruling for slot 8 (it lifts refusals 1–3 and sets the PL2 permit — the cli
   never does), and `risk-reviewer` closing this entry.

### Slot 9, the member (`strategy-pm15`, PM15-5)

- **S16-R5 amended:** slot 9 is built (`BIT_PM15` 0x0200, `BUILT_MASK`
  0x02FF); **`ALL_MASK` = 0x00FF** — `--strategy all` does not include
  pm15, so no existing boot picks it up unasked. Slots 8 and 10–15 stay
  reserved. `/state`, the TUI, the dashboard and `audit_pnl` name slot 9
  `pm15`.
- **The law** (doc 39 §4, frozen): τ ∈ [2, 20) s; the favoured side
  p ≥ 0.90 for 2 consecutive report seconds; an IoC at an ask ≤ p − 0.02;
  at most 4 IoCs per market. *(Amended 2026-10-19 by PMJ J8, ruling
  R-PMJ-S24 — a documented deviation from doc 39 §4: the ask must also be
  at least `price_floor` 0.90, slot 11's floor — and its paper fills
  follow the J8 sweep. P0's count is segmented at the J8 boot (`docs/state.md`
  dates it): the windows before it ran the frozen law and the touch fill,
  the ones after it the amended law and the sweep. See "PMJ — slot 11",
  `### J8`.)* The pricer is `core-twaplock::report`
  (Chainlink reports on their own second, samples [T−60, T−1]).
- **The strike:** the RTDS mean of [open − 60, open − 1] (within 0.1–15
  ppm of the venue's, measured). Gamma publishes a window's `priceToBeat`
  only when that window resolves, so during a window the reports are the
  only source. A window open before the boot has no strike (counted
  `strikes_missing`, `hold_strike`) and is never traded.
- **The caps:** $250 per order, $250 committed per market (fills plus the
  one in flight), the session's realised loss at −$500 halts the member.
  No day cap. *(R-PMJ-S21, 2026-10-19: the session bound is −$3 500 in
  `pm15.toml` from the next boot — and, by R-PM-8, slot 9's live bound once
  armed.)*
- **Paper fills (PM15-5c):** the held-quote law (`core_fill::held`, the
  HC11 law Hypercall's IoCs already use): an IoC fills at the leg's quote
  in force **350 ms after submit** — the activation Δ (200 ms, the
  unmeasured-venue assumption) plus the venue's taker hold (150 ms on its
  crypto markets since 2026-09-04) — at the touch, capped by its size, or
  gets nothing. The strict-cross law it replaces waited for the leg's
  first tick after activation: on a delta feed a quiet leg sends none, so
  an order the venue would fill was cancelled at its TTL. *(PMJ J8,
  R-PMJ-S23: no longer the touch alone — the touch, then the depth lane's
  levels behind it up to the limit, as the venue's FAK; `### J8`.)* The fee
  0.07·p·(1 − p) per share; settlement +1 / 0 per share at
  `market_resolved`. The offline harness has no held law (as for
  Hypercall): slot 9's paper is judged in the engine only.
- **`exec_router::LEDGER_ROWS` 16 → 32:** seven PM families take 14 rows
  (two token pairs each, by window parity) beside bin15's HL families.
- **The bin15 guard:** `strategy_bin15` reads Hyperliquid rolls only — a

### PM15-5c — a quiet book is not a stale one (2026-10-17)

The first paper windows priced and then skipped 385 of 440 evaluations as
"no fresh ask": the member called a touch older than 3 s stale, while the
ingress emits a leg's touch only when it changes — and a favourite at
0.99 in the last 20 s often does not.

- **The ingress re-asserts every touch at each `PONG`** of the market
  socket (a `PING` every 5 s; the socket delivers in order, so every frame
  before the `PONG` has been read): `touches_reasserted`.
- **It withdraws every touch when the session drops** — a stale tick,
  both sides zero — so neither the member nor the paper book trusts a dead
  socket's book: `touches_withdrawn`. *(Amended by PMJ J7, R-PMJ-S19: both
  rules are per market socket — a `PONG` re-asserts, and a lost session
  withdraws, only the touches of the families that socket carries; see
  "PMJ — slot 11", `### J7`.)* The market socket's idle law is 12 s
  (it was 30 s): two missed `PONG`s and a margin, well inside a 20 s late
  window.
- **The member's freshness bound is 8 s** (the `PING` period plus 3 s),
  and the book gate names three reasons: `skip_book` (no ask: none quoted,
  or withdrawn), `skip_book_old` (8 s without a change or a `PONG`),
  `skip_law` (no tick yet).
- **Paper:** the held-quote law above.
- **The published-strike re-read is gone** (PM15-5b's): the venue writes a
  window's `priceToBeat` only once it resolves. `strikes_published` is
  gone with it; a window that opened before the boot stays untradeable
  (`hold_strike`, about one window per family per restart).

Live safety is unchanged by the bound: a FAK is matched by the venue at
its own book, never above the member's limit `p − e`.

### PM15-5d — a re-asserted touch is not judged by its old stamp (`ef8b22c`)

5c's re-assertion carried the leg's last venue stamp, so the feed clock
judged an unchanged touch stale exactly when it was re-asserted. The
re-asserted touch is now stamped `venue_ms = 0` (the clock does not judge
it); the member's own 8 s bound is the only freshness law on it. Seen
since: in the last ~25 s of a window the favourite usually has **no ask
at all** (its bid 0.99 / 0.999) — the remaining `skip_book` is the
venue's book, not the feed.

### PM15-6b — the arm's cores, socket-free (`cc6900b`)

`exec-polymarket`'s three threads' cores, each driven by a test rig:

- **`PmArm`** (the engine's `OrderDispatch` for slot 9): admission —
  slot 9, a rolling leg, its family in `live_families` (⊆ BTC, ETH: D-9),
  an IoC BUY at 0 < p < 1, a free row, not halted; the push is one 64 B
  ring write. Fills only from the user channel's `trade` (E-5), each
  trade id booked once; retirements only after the fills; a `FAILED`
  after a booked match halts the slot.
- **pm-gw** (`PmGateway`): one blocking request per pass — the order
  (SENT before the POST; the retry law D-12), else recon
  (`/data/trades?market=&after=`, paged, at most one per 2 s), else the
  account read. An answer it cannot read is IN DOUBT (the stake held
  until recon), never a release.
- **pm-user** (`PmUserDriver`): the user channel, `PING` every 5 s; a
  session lost asks recon for every open order.

### PM15-6d — redemption through the relayer (R-PM-6, plan D-10)

- **Which legs:** a won leg, or one whose roll settled unknown, is asked
  redeemed once (`CMD_REDEEM`) at the first account read that shows the
  venue holding it. A leg its roll settled against leaves the arm's ledger
  at settlement (worth 0, never redeemed; its tokens stay in the wallet,
  unwatched).
- **Where:** on pm-gw, after the account read in its idle path, one
  request per pass, never in a window's last 30 s (the late law orders
  only there), on its own keep-alive client to
  `relayer-v2.polymarket.com`. No fourth thread: pm-gw holds the token
  table the condition ids come from.
- **The batch:** a market ripens 3 min after its ask; up to 8 ripe markets
  go in one Deposit Wallet `Batch` the owner signs (deadline + 240 s):
  the wallet's nonce (`GET /v1/account/transactions/params`), `POST
  /submit`, then `GET /v1/account/transactions/<id>` every 2 s. `MINED` /
  `CONFIRMED` redeem the batch; `FAILED` / `INVALID`, a refused submit or
  90 polls without a terminal state cost each market a try, and a market
  is dropped after three (redeem it by hand). The quota answer (429) costs
  no try; a failed request waits 5 min. The boot's first batch begins with
  `CTF.setApprovalForAll(CtfCollateralAdapter, true)`; each market is
  `CtfCollateralAdapter.redeemPositions(pUSD, 0, condition, [1, 2])`.
- **The ledger:** a redeemed leg leaves when its venue balance reads 0;
  that read is not judged (its pUSD may predate the credit) — the next
  one is.
- **Never a halt:** an unredeemed leg is worth its cost in the arm's
  ledger (conservative); no order depends on the redemption.
- **The boot:** signature type 3 with `PM15_RELAYER_API_KEY`, proved by
  reading the wallet's relayer nonce; `PM15_REDEEM=hand` boots without a
  redeemer (asks counted, `redeem_off`); any other signature type refuses
  unless redemption is by hand. `pm-exec --key-check` reads the nonce too.
- **Pinned:** spec J.4's batch (the approval and one market; digest
  `fdd9b2c8…34b3`, signature `5dc1610b…711c`) and a second batch (two
  markets, nonce 31), both re-derived by an independent EIP-712 library
  (eth-account 0.14); J.4 runs in the boot self-test. Alloc gate 131: a
  full batch cycle at 0 B.

### PM15-6e — the operator's tools: the checks, the miss probe, the flip

- **`scripts/pm15-exec.sh self-test | key-check | miss-probe`** runs
  `multivenue-engine pm-exec` with slot 9's account sourced from the repo
  `.env` into the binary's environment (the script prints none of it):
  the pinned vectors (offline); the venue gate read-only with the
  relayer key proved; and **the miss probe — ONE order**: a $1 FAK BUY
  on BTC's current window priced at the tick, on the leg whose lowest ask
  is the higher, sent through pm-gw's own submit path. It refuses with
  under 5 min left in the window or a lowest ask under 0.05 on that leg,
  so it cannot fill; the venue's "no match" answer proves the order's
  signature, its amounts and the clock (spec K.1, K.13) with nothing
  bought. Any other answer is reported (an acceptance or a doubt costs at
  most $1).
- **`scripts/pm15-flip.sh status | live | paper`** edits only
  `[exec.slot.9]` and `ARM_LIVE` / `EXEC_TOML` (stamped backups), sets
  the session anchor aside (every `live` starts a new session) and
  restarts nothing: the next gated restart applies it. The live section
  is R-PM-8's frame — $250 an order and a market, `halt_on_loss` $500,
  `max_open_orders` 8, `halt_on_recon_stale_ms` 180 000 (the account read
  pauses in each window's quiet tail and skips judging the read that sees
  a redemption), and `cap_day_usd_1e6` **$100 000, out of reach** (two
  live families × 96 windows × $250 = $48 000 a UTC day; the config law
  refuses 0). A test pins that the section resolves through the
  interlock at those numbers.
- **`live` refuses** unless the committed risk policy has a line that
  begins with the gate word — `PM15-LIVE-GATE: P0 PASS` for P0's result,
  or `PM15-LIVE-GATE: ruled` for an operator ruling (R-PM-1); this entry
  quotes them mid-line, so it opens nothing — `pm15.toml` exists and
  `STRATEGY` names pm15, `exec.HALT` does not name slot 9, and the key
  check passes.

### PM15-7 — PolyBolt, dormant (R-PM-3)

- **Why:** RTDS's price topics — the strike's and the pricer's source
  today — are "legacy for reference prices" since PolyBolt's launch
  (2026-09-15); no removal date is announced. PolyBolt
  (`wss://ws-live-v2.polymarket.com/ws`) serves `price.crypto` (Chainlink
  by default since 2026-10-02) and `price.crypto.twap` (the 60-s TWAP the
  markets settle on) behind an `op: auth` frame with the account's CLOB
  API credentials.
- **Built:** `ingress_polymarket::polybolt` — the auth and subscribe
  frames rendered in place, and the parser of a report into RTDS's own
  record (`full_accuracy_value` when present, else `value` quoted or
  bare, each rounded half up from its digits; a stamp in Unix ms or ISO
  8601 UTC; the channel's `seq` and `dropped`). RTDS's 18-decimal
  conversion is shared (`rtds::fav_px`). Alloc gate 132: the frames and
  the parse at 0 B.
- **Dormant:** nothing in the engine reads it. The shapes are the
  migration guide's; the raw frames need credentials.
  `scripts/pm15-exec.sh polybolt-probe [--assets btc,eth] [--seconds N]`
  (`multivenue-engine pm15-polybolt-probe`) prints them live — the first
  frames raw (one naming the API key withheld), the per-asset price and
  TWAP every 10 s — before PolyBolt becomes slot 9's mark, which is its
  own cut and its own entry here.

### PM15-8c — the live arm on `/metrics`

`exec_polymarket::stats::PmExecStats`: one block of relaxed atomics per
writer, each on its own cache lines — the arm (engine thread: its 25
tallies, then halted, reconciled, the account's worth, the anchor, the
drift) and pm-gw (its 17 tallies, the redeemer's 10, then halted) —
published at most once a second, mirrored as `engine_pm15_arm_*` and
`engine_pm15_gw_*` (a tally `…_total`, a level bare). A paper boot never
builds the arm: the family reads 0. The dashboard's slot-9 panel shows the
arm's rows once it is live (submitted, acks, refused, in doubt, fills,
reads, the worth against the anchor, the drift, the redemptions).

### PM15-6f — a restart keeps the legs the account holds

Before it, a restart emptied the arm's ledger: a held leg vanished from
the worth — a false loss against the restored session anchor — and a won
leg was never redeemed.

- **pm-gw's held table** (`exec_polymarket::held`, ≤ 32 legs — the arm's
  ledger size; `WATCH_MAX` 16 → 32, and a full table refuses instead of
  evicting): every leg the arm holds, from its `CMD_WATCH` at each fill
  (shares and cost), its `CMD_REDEEM` at settlement (won / unknown) and
  its `WATCH_STOP` when the leg leaves — with the token's decimal id and
  the market's condition copied while the window's row exists, so the
  reads and the redemption outlive the token table.
- **`pm15-held.state`** beside `exec.toml`: the table written whole
  (through a temporary, renamed) at each change, on pm-gw's idle path,
  never in a window's quiet tail (a failed write retries in 30 s).
- **The boot** restores it to both: the arm's ledger (at cost; a settled
  leg as it was left) and pm-gw's reads and redemption (a settled leg
  asked again). Another account's file refuses the boot. A new session's
  anchor is the pUSD plus the inherited legs at cost.
- **A leg the restarted engine will never see settle** (its window ended
  before the boot; the ingress tracks the current and next ones) is
  expired 900 s after its window's end — after the ingress's own
  10-minute retirement, so a settlement the engine sees always comes
  first: asked redeemed and told to the arm (`EVT_EXPIRED`), which books
  it settled unknown, at 0; its later zero balance reads as redeemed,
  never as a drift.

  then P0's result or a ruling, then `pm15-flip.sh live`.

### J1b — the 5-minute pool, its pipeline, the depth capture

- **The pool** (`core_types::pm_roll`): ordinals 4160 + 7·g + offset
  (`[up0][down0][up1][down1][up2][down2][mark]`), above the whole 15-minute
  pool; window `w` on pair `w mod 3`, so a pair is needed again 600 s after
  its window ends and the 540 s retirement frees it 60 s ahead. Instance ids
  `0x8000_0000 | (window5 · 8 + g)`: a 5-minute id can never equal a
  15-minute one. `PmPeriod` serves the shared code; its 15-minute answers are
  the 15-minute free functions (a test pins each).
- **The universe:** `updown:<asset>:5m`; a family's index is its rank among
  its period's keys, so adding 5-minute keys moves no 15-minute family (a
  test compares every 15-minute manifest row of a mixed universe with the
  15-minute-only one). Each period has its own cap of 8.
- **The pipeline:** a second instance of the rolling ingress, driven for
  the 5-minute period: its own discovery (`pm5-discovery`, two windows
  ahead, the `-updown-5m-` slug and the `5m` settlement law), its own market
  and RTDS sockets (`ingress-pm5`; at most 42 tokens subscribed), tick and
  event lane 9 (`engine::PM5_LANE`), the `pm5` capture, raw-tap label and
  `/metrics` family. It spawns only when `[polymarket] rolling` names a
  `:5m` key. No gateway tee: slot 9's arm never sees a 5-minute window.
- **Slot 9 is untouched by the 5-minute records** (R-PMJ-3): `strategy-pm15`
  returns on any 5-minute sym before its roll, order-law, mark and touch
  paths — no order, no market, no counter changes (a test). Its boot and the
  15-minute spawn read the `:15m` keys only.
- **The router ledger: `LEDGER_ROWS` 32 → 64** (`Ledger` 161 408 B). It
  binds every roll it sees, keyed (venue, family byte), and refuses a family
  byte at or above its row count; the 5-minute bytes reach 39, and at the
  caps the table holds HL's 8 + PM 15 m's 16 + PM 5 m's 24 rows. **This is
  the live router of slot 3:** the risk checks scan the rows, so the
  per-order cost grows by the 32 empty rows' bound test.
- **The depth capture** (month results, caveat 3): the rolling ingress never
  wrote `pm15-depth.pmlr`; it now writes a top-5 `DepthTopK` per leg,
  best first from the venue's touch, change-gated through a `DepthPair` (the
  spare row written in place, flipped on a change), whenever the leg's slot
  ticks, for both periods. Capture only: no depth lane carries it. A level
  whose size the ladder does not know is not written.
- **The Gamma market id** joins `PmWindowSpec` (`market_id`): Jupiter names
  its markets `POLY-<market id>-<0|1>`. A non-decimal id reads 0; it can
  never refuse a static market row.
- **Gates:** see the J1b gate line below.

### J2 — base58, the raw Ed25519 signature, verification, the Solana keypair (R-PMJ-S3)

- **No new dependency.** Ed25519 stays on `ring` in `signer-ed25519`
  (O-BX5); `core-crypto` stays dependency-free.
- `core_crypto::base58_decode` / `base58_encode`: the Bitcoin alphabet,
  zero-alloc (the working number lives in the caller's buffer), boot and
  cold paths only — **not constant-time**, so it may decode a secret only at
  boot (the wallet key), never on a path an observer can time.
- `Ed25519Signer::sign_raw`: the 64-byte signature written into the
  caller's slot (the transaction's own buffer); `verify`: `ring`'s strict
  RFC 8032 verification; `Ed25519Signer::from_solana_keypair`: a wallet's
  64-byte export (seed ‖ public key) — the seed expanded into the locked
  page as `from_seed`, the local seed copy wiped, and a public half the seed
  does not derive refused (`KeypairMismatch`, compared in constant time).
- The boot self-test (LAW BX-3) now also checks every RFC 8032 vector's raw
  signature and its verification both ways; Binance's arm runs the same
  self-test, so its boot checks more and accepts nothing new.
- **Gates:** `make lint` rc 0 · nextest (core-crypto, signer-ed25519,
  exec-binance, exec-polymarket) 457 passed · gate 86 at 0 B with `sign_raw`
  + `verify` in its loop (the self-test's allocation count unchanged: one
  page per vector) · copy-audit new 0 · license OK.


### J3 — `exec-jupiter`: the guard, jup-gw, slot 11's arm (built and rig-tested; never armed)

- **The venue (R-PMJ-S2): `VenueId::Jupiter` = 10, `VENUE_COUNT` 11.** An
  execution route with no market data: no tick, depth, option or fill lane;
  staleness 0 (never judged); the paper activation and the harness latency
  0 — dead like `Ai`, and never tradeable in the harness
  (`tradeable_venue_byte` is unchanged). `exec.toml` spells it `jupiter`.
- **The router lists gain Jupiter** (`LIVE_ARM_VENUES`,
  `PNL_JUDGING_VENUES`), **and refusals precede them:** a live slot 11
  refuses the boot until a `PMJ-DUST-GATE` line here; a live slot naming
  `jupiter` that is not slot 11 refuses ("whose only arm is slot 11's"); a
  paper slot naming it arms nothing. The binary-contract risk law
  (`px·qty/1e6`) is unchanged.
- **LAW PMJ-G — never sign a server-built transaction blind.** Jupiter's
  `POST /orders` answers an unsigned Solana transaction; jup-gw decodes it
  into a fixed 1 232 B buffer and signs it only when every line holds:
  the fee payer is our wallet and our wallet is a required signer; every
  invoked program is in `pmj.toml`'s `guard_programs` and is a static key
  (never loaded from a lookup table); every lookup table is in
  `guard_alts`; **the transaction requires exactly one signature — ours** (a
  co-signer could hold it; checked on the transaction, not only on the
  answer's `requiredSigners`); **no System `AdvanceNonceAccount`, whatever
  it names** (a durable-nonce transaction never expires, so the server
  could land it whenever it liked); the SPL Token / Token-2022 `Transfer`
  / `TransferChecked` our wallet authorises come **from the deposit
  account** (`guard_deposit_account`, the wallet's USDC account — none configured
  refuses every debit; one loaded through a lookup table is refused) and,
  checked, **in the deposit mint**, and sum to at most the `depositAmount`
  we asked (0 for a claim), with our wallet the authority and nothing
  else; any other Token
  instruction our wallet takes part in (`Approve`, `SetAuthority`,
  `CloseAccount`, `Burn` …) is refused; System transfers and account funding from
  our keys at most `guard_max_sol_lamports`; the compute-unit price at most
  `guard_max_cu_price` (so a transaction's fees are bounded by 5 000 lamports
  for the one signature plus `max_cu_price` × at most 1.4 M units — 0.07
  mSOL at a 50 000 µlamport cap — plus `guard_max_sol_lamports`).
  The answer must be the order we asked — `requiredSigners` exactly our
  wallet, `order.marketId` the window's `POLY-<id>-<o>`, `isYes` and
  `isBuy` true, `userPubkey` our wallet, `orderCostUsd` within the deposit
  — and the server's price cap (`maxBuyPriceUsd`, the answer's word) at
  most the member's limit (`p − 2c`); else the build is refused unsigned. **An empty allowlist
  refuses everything**, and is the default until J0's decoded programs and
  tables are reviewed into the `guard_*` keys. **The guard's limit: a CPI's debits
  are invisible before signing** — an allowlisted program is trusted with
  whatever the transaction's accounts let it reach; the program allowlist
  is what bounds that. **Its consequence (risk review, 2026-10-18):**
  Jupiter's own program most likely moves the deposit itself (a CPI,
  not a top-level transfer); if so, the "≤ `depositAmount`" line binds
  nothing, the per-order maximum and the session bound are not enforced
  before signing, and the real bound is the wallet's USDC. **Before a
  `PMJ-DUST-GATE` line, this section must require:** (a) the wallet holds
  at most the slot's day cap in USDC; (b) J0 decodes Jupiter's
  create-order instruction data so the guard checks its amount (and its
  price) itself; (c) a halt when the wallet's USDC falls by more than the
  deposit plus the fee after an order lands.
- **jup-gw** (`exec_jupiter::gw`, socket-free; `core_net::HttpsReq` in
  production): build → guard → sign (our signature written into its own
  slot) → `POST /execute` with the build's `context` verbatim → LANDED /
  REFUSED / IN DOUBT → `GET /orders/status/{pk}` every 250 ms until
  terminal or the window's close + 30 s → recon (`GET /orders`, the order's
  `filledContracts` and `avgFillPriceUsd`) → FILL (cumulative) and DONE.
  **E-5 for this venue:** the execute's `Success` is the ACK; the order
  record's fill numbers are the FILL. Fail closed: a build creates nothing
  on chain, so any failure before the execute is a refusal; **every
  execute answer but `Success` came after the signed transaction left the
  host and is not believed** — `Failed`, a 4xx (a region or a key refusal
  still halts), an unreadable or absent answer are in doubt, polled like
  an unanswered one, and released (DONE, never landed) only once its
  blockhash has surely expired (300 s after the execute; ~150 blocks live
  60–90 s) AND recon read every page without finding it — pages left
  unread are no evidence; a terminal record without its fill quantity (or
  a filled one without its price) is not read, never booked unfilled; an
  order — landed, or in doubt with pages left unread — that recon cannot
  read for 30 tries is LOST and halts. **Recon reads 4 pages of 50**: if
  `/orders` lists oldest first, an account past 200 orders would LOSE (and
  halt on) every in-doubt order — J5 pages deeper or queries by time
  before arming. **Execute-stage refusals count toward the reject-streak
  halt** (`halt_on_reject_streak`): a `Failed` or a 4xx at the execute
  raises the streak while its row stays in doubt; a landing resets it. The
  build's `lastValidBlockHeight` is not used (no chain height is read in
  this pass).
- **Halts** (the duplex's halt word): a region refusal, an authentication
  refusal, a lost order, a lost event, the arm's own (an event of no
  order, a full queue or ledger, a fill price off the binary law: it halts
  jup-gw too, so a queued intent is refused unbuilt), and the operator's —
  **`exec.HALT`
  on slot 11 reaches the arm's `cancel_slot`, which halts jup-gw's builds**;
  a landed keeper order cannot be pulled, so it is still polled and
  reconciled to its end (`cancel_slot_state` answers Working until then).
- **The arm** (`exec_jupiter::arm`, an `OrderDispatch`): slot 11 only;
  `Order.venue` = Jupiter; a 5-minute leg (R-PMJ-3) of a family allowed
  live, on the window its order law is in force for; an IoC BUY at
  `0 < px < 1`; a deposit `px·qty/1e6` of at least the venue's $5 and at
  most the per-order maximum (`pmj.toml`); no cancel, no modify. Its worth
  for the session bound: the wallet's USDC plus each unclaimed leg at cost,
  a leg its roll settled as lost at 0; the anchor at the first balance read
  (or the boot's).
- **Claims are held, not sent:** jup-gw reads the positions, builds each
  claimable one's claim, guards it (no token may leave our account) and
  signs it — and stops: **the claim's submission route is unverified until
  J0 records one** (and no claim is built while jup-gw is halted). A won
  leg therefore stays in the worth at cost — until the positions read
  shows it claimed (or settled by the venue on its own, `settlement:
  auto`): then it leaves both ledgers, its payout in the USDC. Between a
  balance read that already holds the payout and the positions read that
  removes the leg (≤ 60 s), the worth is overstated by the leg's cost.
  J5 wires the route before any arming.
- **Wire facts to verify at J0 (before J5):** the market id
  `POLY-<Gamma id>-<0|1>` with `isYes: true` for a buy of either outcome;
  `requiredSigners` = our wallet alone on a keeper order; the `/orders`
  record's `filledContracts` / `avgFillPriceUsd` spelling and units; the
  `/positions` envelope; the balances read (`GET /ultra/v1/balances/{wallet}`,
  `amount` in base units, `SOL` for the native coin); the claim route;
  whether a venue-settled position reads `claimed`, and what the build's
  `settlement: auto` means.
- **HTTPS:** one keep-alive connection to `api.jup.ag` through
  `core_net::HttpsReq` (HttpsConn's raw form) rather than HttpsConn
  templates — a template's query form always renders `path?`, so the two
  path-parameter requests fit none; the `x-api-key` header is fixed at boot
  in the gateway's own buffer (wiped on drop). Two copies are not wiped:
  the request buffer `HttpsReq` renders each head into, and the caller's
  environment read (J5's wiring).
- **Boot checks:** jup-gw refuses a guard for another wallet, a signer
  that is not the wallet, an API key a header cannot carry, a short body
  window; the arm refuses any slot but 11; both refuse a per-order maximum
  under $5, and the boot (J5) builds both from one `pmj.toml` key. The
  live-slot-11 refusal in `exec_boot` is unreachable until J4 gives slot
  11 its `BUILT_MASK` bit (S16-R5 refuses it first): J4 pins it with a
  test in the same commit.
- **Secrets:** `JUP_API_KEY` and `PMJ_WALLET_KEY` reach the process only
  through the wrapper sourcing `.env` (J5's wiring: slot 11 paper builds no
  arm and reads neither). The wallet key loads through
  `Ed25519Signer::from_solana_keypair` into the locked page.
- **Gauges:** the arm's and jup-gw's `/metrics` words (`engine_pmj_arm_*`,
  `engine_pmj_gw_*`: refusals by reason, the USDC and SOL gauges); the
  latencies in the duplex's fixed series — `push_to_write` decision → build,
  `post_rtt` the build, `rest_rtt` the land, `cancel_rtt` a status poll,
  `fill_venue_to_local` execute → fill read.
- **Risk review** (an Opus subagent at xhigh, read-only, three rounds):

  | round | verdict | findings → resolution |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | BLOCK | MAJOR: recon running out of pages read as "never landed"; the signer count checked on the answer only (a durable nonce); a token debit's source and mint unchecked; a balance without USDC read as 0; a terminal record without its quantity booked 0; NEEDS-DOCS: the CPI-deposit consequence. MINOR: a 4xx execute freed its row; the 120 s blockhash rule; the build not cross-checked; the arm's halt not stopping jup-gw; claimed legs never leaving; the fee bound unstated. NITs: boot checks, claims while halted, key copies, the signing-key bullet | each fixed in code with a named test (`hostile_a_second_required_signer_is_refused`, `hostile_a_durable_nonce_advance_is_refused_whatever_it_names`, `hostile_a_debit_from_another_account_or_mint_is_refused`, `recon_that_runs_out_of_pages_never_releases_an_in_doubt_order`, `a_terminal_record_without_its_numbers_is_retried_never_booked_unfilled`, `a_balance_answer_without_usdc_is_a_failed_read`, `an_execute_refused_with_a_4xx_is_in_doubt_and_a_region_refusal_still_halts`, `a_build_for_another_order_is_refused_unsigned`, `the_arm_boots_only_for_slot_11_and_its_own_halt_stops_the_gateway`, `a_claimed_position_leaves_the_held_table_and_tells_the_arm`, `no_claim_is_built_while_halted`), or written above (the CPI consequence and its three pre-dust requirements, the fee bound, the key copies) |

### J4 — `strategy-pmj`, slot 11's member (PAPER)
- **The member** (`crates/strategy-pmj`) trades slot 9's H90 law on the
  5-minute pool only (the `pm5_*` syms; instance ids carry bit 31; a
  15-minute record is ignored, R-PMJ-3). **The law is duplicated, not
  shared:** the crate is `strategy-pm15` copied and adapted, so slot 9 —
  armable — stays bit for bit; the cost is two copies to keep in step until
  the 5-minute research (R5) freezes its own law, and a change to pm15's law
  is NOT a change to pmj's. PMJ's own keys: the **price floor** (the
  favourite's ask ≥ 0.90, else `skip_price`); the **keeper's lead** (`τ ≥
  max(tau_min, min_tau)`, 3 s); the **$5 deposit** (sized up to $5 plus one
  share step, never past the market's room — under $5 of room, no order);
  the **paper fee** at twice Polymarket's taker fee (`2 × 0.07·p·(1 − p)`
  per share: the keeper's and Jupiter's — MEASURED from the venue before
  any arming, never read from a doc). Orders: an IoC BUY of the favourite,
  `VenueId::Jupiter`, the Polymarket leg's sym.
- **The paper law** (the plan's keeper-aware law): the held-quote book
  (`core_fill::held`) carries the 5-minute legs after the 15-minute ones; a
  5-minute IoC is judged against the touch held at its submit +
  `paper_delay_ms` (2 s default, `pmj.toml`;
  `PaperDispatcher::with_pm5_held_delay_ns`) — the keeper's latency, not the
  CLOB's *(PMJ J8: the touch and the levels behind it, the FAK sweep,
  `### J8`)*. The 15-minute legs keep pm15's delay. The delay is bounded by the
  keeper's lead (`paper_delay_ms` < max(`tau_min`, `min_tau_s`), else the
  parse refuses): an order decided at the window's floor is still judged
  before the close, never against a book the venue has closed. The pending
  IoCs have a share per class (`core_fill::held::HELD_PENDING_SHARES`: 16
  options, 8 15-minute legs, 8 5-minute legs — one per family, a member
  holding at most one IoC per family): a burst of slot 11's or slot 7's
  never refuses slot 9's take (the book's 16 were shared before J4).
- **A miss frees its market on the member's timer, not at the verdict:**
  like slot 9's member, slot 11's keeps the trait's no-op for the
  dispatcher's `CANCELED`/`EXPIRED` order event, so an IoC that does not
  fill blocks its market until `2 × order_ttl` (10 s) — about 60 % of the
  late window — and `max_orders_market` is rarely reached. The paper run
  is that law's, conservatively; changing it for slot 11 alone would part
  the two copies (above) and is a ruling, not a J4 fix.
- **The artifact** `~/multivenue/pmj.toml` (`core_config::pmj`: one `[pmj]`
  section, every bound at parse, the bytes hashed into the boot tell
  `pmj: artifact configured (PAPER) …`). Read only when `--strategy` names
  `pmj`; a request without it aborts the boot; `families` must equal the
  universe's 5-minute `[polymarket] rolling` list in order; `pmj-check`
  validates it offline. `PMJ_TOML=<path>` in `strategy.conf` names another
  (`scripts/engine-wrapper.sh`, the `XMM_TOML` shape: a file, and `STRATEGY`
  must carry `pmj`, else exit 78). A `pm15.toml` copied whole refuses (its section, its
  `usd_order_1e6`, no deposit). Its H90 values are pm15's, provisional (R5).
- **The frame (paper; the dust frame R-PMJ-5 names for J5):** the deposit
  $5 per order; `usd_market` $10 per market; the session loss bound −$50
  (at or below it the member enters nothing for the session: `skip_halt`,

  order written off at 2 × ttl). Parse bounds: deposit and market

### J6 — the rolling depth capture, bounded (2026-10-19, ruling R-PMJ-S15)
- **Why:** J1b's rolling depth capture (`pm15-depth.pmlr` + `pm5-depth.pmlr`)
  recorded every top-5-per-side change of every leg — ~1.35 GB/h at 7 + 7
  families, half the run dir's ~2.7 GB/h (the operator's Mac, 2026-10-18) —
  and the disk fell to 3.6 GiB free (relieved by the S3 push and cleanup at
  19:35–20:00Z and 2026-10-19 03:15–03:22Z).
- **The rule:** `[polymarket] rolling_depth` (default on) and
  `rolling_depth_ms` (default 1000, 0..=60000; 0 = every change, J1b's
  stream bit for bit): a leg's records are at least the spacing apart, a
  new window's first book is not held by the spacing (it is written at its
  first book or change once the slot goes live), and a change
  the spacing held is written by the first market `PONG` sweep at least the
  spacing after the leg's last record — so at most spacing + 5 s late (~6 s
  at the default). That is a departure from the ruling's "the next PONG",
  made to keep the one-record-per-spacing cap. A sweep record carries the
  PONG's arrival time. A held change is lost when the leg stops ticking
  before the sweep (its window resolves or retires, its slot breaks, or the
  market session drops and the ladders clear) — at most the last spacing +
  5 s of a window; the first book after a reconnect (not a rebind) waits for
  the spacing too. Capture only: no lane, member, cap, halt or law reads
  depth; the ticks and events are identical under every policy, on the
  replay and on the PONG sweep (pinned by
  `the_depth_capture_keeps_one_record_per_leg_per_second_and_the_sweep_catches_up`).
- **The market sockets (diagnosed, not changed):** Polymarket closes the
  rolling market sockets with **1013 "slow consumer: send buffer full"**
  (on 2026-10-19 00:11–03:25Z: pm5 111×, pm15 42×). A standalone probe on
  its own connection (12 tokens; vault `docs/research/pmj/j5probe/`, logs in
  `~/multivenue/research/pmj/ws-close-*.log`) saw the same code on its
  dynamically re-subscribing connection (after 65–367 s) while its static
  one held 868 s — consistent with a venue-side per-connection limit at the
  5-minute books' message rate, but not conclusive: the probe's own stalls
  (synchronous discovery calls) and this host's receive side are not
  excluded, nor is J1b's per-change depth work on the ingress thread. Each
  close withdraws the touches until the resubscribe. **To do:** re-count
  the closes per hour after J6 deploys; the remedies (the subscription
  sharded over several sockets, or a larger kernel receive buffer — a new
  dependency) are their own ruling.
- **Risk review** (an Opus subagent at xhigh, read-only, three rounds): 1
  NEEDS-DOCS (the new test never reached the PONG sweep — its fixture's
  last frame resolves the window; the 1013 diagnosis overstated; "≤ 5 s"
  wrong, it is spacing + 5 s; the loss when a leg stops ticking; the
  readers' note; the ruling row) → the test rewritten to search a cut that
  holds a change back and to pin ticks and events identical on the replay
  and the sweep, the docs corrected; 2 BLOCK (the rewritten test did not
  compile: `ChannelEvent` has no `PartialEq`) → compared by its fields; 3
  **APPROVE**, on the conditions that bench-check's reds be judged by an
  A/B against HEAD (R-PMJ-S6) and that the restart keep the restart law.
